messages.subject: multilevel model with group-level predictors
parts:
Hello folks: 
I am trying to estimate a fairly simple multilevel model with group-level predictors for the intercept and randomly varying predictor variables. When I adapted code from the radon example (ARM/ch 16/radon.2) it runs fine. In this example, the group-level model is written as:

  for (j in 1:J)
    a[j] ~ normal(g_0 + g_1 * u[j], sigma_a);

I want to re-express this in matrix terms so that it can more easily accommodate multiple group-level predictors. This should be simple--I've done it lots of times in Bugs--and the model compiles okay but then bogs down, iterating so slowly that it is clear there is something wrong. Here is the model, with the key lines in blue:  


data {
  int<lower=0> N;                // num country-years
  int<lower=0> J;                // num countries
  int<lower=0> K;                // num level 1 predictors
  int<lower=0> M;                // num level 2 predictors
  int<lower=1> cid[N];           // country id
  vector[N] y;                   // outcome
  matrix[N,K] xmat;              // level 1 predictors
  matrix[J,M] zmat;              // level 2 predictors
}

parameters {
  real beta0[J];                 // country intercepts
  vector[K] beta[J];             // country coefficients
  real B0[M];                    // intercept coefficients
  vector[K] B;                   // effects coefficients
  real<lower=0> sigma_b0;        // intercept variance
  real<lower=0> sigma_b[K];      // parameter variances
  real<lower=0> sigma_y[J];      // y heteroscedastic
}

model {
  for (j in 1:J)                 // model for intercept
    for (m in 1:M)
    beta0[j] ~ normal(zmat[j,m] * B0[m], sigma_b0);
  for (j in 1:J)                 // varying effects coefficients
    for (k in 1:K) 
      beta[j,k] ~ normal(B[k], sigma_b[k]);

  for (n in 1:N)
    y[n] ~ normal(beta0[cid[n]] + xmat[n] * beta[cid[n]], 
      sigma_y[cid[n]]);

  B0 ~ cauchy(0, 2);
  sigma_b0 ~ cauchy(0, 2);
  B ~  cauchy(0, 2);

}

Note that zmat has ones in the first column. I would be grateful if someone would point out how I'm screwing this up. 

Best,
Jack
